title: Original timestamp conversions, skew, calendar and day cache state
oracle: Literal signed32/2038/unit-heuristic/hex-long thresholds, RFC UTC date strings, Python datetime/isocalendar/zoneinfo calendar facts and exact source-state cache timelines. Generated ToInt32 expectations use BigInt modular arithmetic with a separate sentinel exclusion rather than archived bitwise conversion; millisecond multiplication uses BigInt rounding and elapsed-day ceilings use integer division. No expected value is obtained by executing WA source. Only the actual original module runs in the selected subject; no time or cache implementation is mocked.

exclusions: All8present original transitive source modules are inventoried at bothpins; no supported gate reads found. Missing cr6640 keeps original closure incomplete, and gates outside this caller scope are not covered. One empty synthetic assignment is not a complete configuration-independence proof.
Explicit cr6640:null selects the real archived Promise fallback. Original substitution provider and bundle bootstrap remain unproven; no timestamp, conversion, calendar or cache helper is replaced.
Signed conversion wraps via ToInt32 before excluding reserved minimum; source edge behavior is characterized rather than corrected. Post2038 values do not establish protocol date support.
Clock skew and timezone are explicit synthetic execution context, not server-delivered clock synchronization or real account state.

sameDay epoch-zero sentinel, skew-stale cache and fixed86400second cutoff are documented source-state characterizations, not desired calendar-equivalence claims. Repeated/reversed calls preserve actual cache lifetime.

No delayUntil, setTimeout, event loop delay, performance.now, monotonicTime, monotonicTimeSince or MonotonicTimer acceptance. The misleadingly named performanceAbsoluteNow is actual Date.now and is wall-clock-controlled.

weekOfYear nominal ISO-week tables use midnight UTC dates. Original code retains subday time before a ceiling, so2016/2021Jan4 at00:00:00.001 or noon returns2 rather than nominal ISOweek1; a separate literal boundary table characterizes this source behavior without claiming general ISO correctness.

Numeric/string/date domains and sequences are unbounded. Finite grids, three timezones, selected DST and ISO-week facts do not prove every JavaScript coercion, timezone database version or execution history.
Signed negative-zero transport is not supported or asserted. Invalid Date observation uses getTime projection to avoid treating snapshot toISOString failure as a vendor rejection.
No network, storage, background expiry, browser, native session, customer account, provider service, cryptographic operation or named-library behavior is exercised.
Alternative module variants, production containers and isolated authored-TS scheduling remain unexercised; diagnostic process runs must report isolated:false.
